given.note: Another world for the demo owner of commit-event-id-checked.json, beside commit-event-control-proven.json's (README v1.14 default 232): the user, as Rosie's team on staging, decides S1-75's control item (review-s1-75-demo-up-1) done with controlProven true an hour after the upload, while the owner is still answering the setup questions, so S1-29's terms consent is not written and the walk has not reached S1-32. The decision writes business_setup's control as decideReviewItem does (default 215) and hands the event {control_proven, S1-32, review-s1-75-demo-up-1} to the owner's own chat handle actor (E10, A18), which runs it as a turn of its own. The gate finds the turn id not committed before (default 222) and reads the key's own source (default 224): the item is the owner's, of the turn's business, decided done proving control, but S1-29's terms consent is not written, so S1-32 is not waiting (given.eventSource waiting false). It answers eventNotWaiting, naming the key and the step alone, and writes nothing: no row, no walk, no turn row. eventNotWaiting is final: the runtime does not resend or rerun it, parks nothing and sends nothing, and the event is dropped (default 230). Nothing is lost: when the owner's own turn later walks to S1-32, its reach settler reads the control written, and answers 'Confirmed in minutes' in that turn (R22). The two worlds' ids are each fixture's own stand-ins (README v1.5 default 131): here the event and the turn are the early ones.
